channel.description: Recent content in Blog on Marcus Poon | Quality Professional

item.title: Exercise Changes Your Brain: What Neuroscience Says and How to Start Today
item.description: Neuroscience proves exercise changes brain chemistry, structure, and function. A practical guide to using movement as a tool for focus, mood, and cognitive performance.

item.title: The 5 Second Rule: How a Simple Countdown Can Beat Procrastination
item.description: Mel Robbins' 5 Second Rule uses neuroscience to overcome procrastination. A simple countdown that transforms how you act in life and work.

item.title: Ray Dalio's Extreme Transparency and How It Applies to Quality Work
item.description: Ray Dalio built the world's largest hedge fund on extreme transparency. Here is what quality professionals can learn from his radical approach to honest feedback and open communication.

item.title: Sam Walton Ten-Foot Rule
item.description: Sam Waltons Ten-Foot Rule transformed employee engagement into retail dominance through genuine human connection.

item.title: Pixar's Braintrust: The Power of Candor Without Ego
item.description: How Pixar's Braintrust meetings built a culture of honest feedback without ego, delivering better creative outcomes.

item.title: The Weight of an Empty Bucket
item.description: A production manager reveals how carrying empty buckets all day exhausts workers — and what it teaches us about cognitive load, emotional baggage, and the art of letting go.

item.title: Akio Toyoda: Building People Before Building Cars
item.description: The story of Akio Toyoda, the racing driver who became CEO of the worlds largest automaker, and his philosophy that building people comes before building cars.

item.title: First Principles Thinking: Piercing Through Appearances to Reach the Essence
item.description: How first principles thinking powers breakthrough innovation — from Aristotle's archai through Descartes' doubt to Elon Musk's $80/kWh battery revolution, with the three cognitive traps that block most people.

item.title: Supercommunicators: Mastering the 3 Communication Channels
item.description: Charles Duhigg's framework for unlocking connection: practical, emotional, and social conversations — and why matching the right channel is the secret of supercommunicators.

item.title: Why Can They Be So Confident? — The Dunning-Kruger Effect in Chinese Internet Culture
item.description: A deep analysis of An Senyao's viral video on why ignorant people are supremely confident, exploring the Dunning-Kruger Effect, the Puxinnan phenomenon, and overconfidence psychology.

item.title: The Feynman Learning Method 2.0 — Learn Anything Faster with AI
item.description: How to upgrade Richard Feynman's classic 4-step learning technique with AI tools and prompt engineering for faster, deeper learning.

item.title: Six Wealth Cognitions from a Viral Tianya Post — Fact-Checked
item.description: A deep fact-check of six wealth cognitions from a viral Tianya post, cross-referenced with academic research from Naval Ravikant to Walter Mischel.

item.title: Structured Expression: The Art of Speaking to the Point
item.description: A comprehensive guide to structured expression: pyramid principles, seven frameworks (PREP, STAR, FABE, SCQA, AIDA, SPIN, GPEC), workplace templates, and a 30-day training plan.

item.title: The Power of Review: Turning Experience into Ability
item.description: A comprehensive guide to the review methodology: U-shaped learning cycle, five misconceptions, practical templates, and a 30-day habit plan for work and life.

item.title: The Day 1 Philosophy - Why Speed Beats Perfection Every Time
item.description: Reid Hoffman launched LinkedIn with an embarrassingly basic interface. His Day 1 philosophy proves that speed, not perfection, is the ultimate competitive advantage.

item.title: 99% of Learning Is Self-Deception - Lessons from 'Learn How to Learn'
item.description: A deep analysis of the book 'Learn How to Learn' by Liu Lan - why 99% of conventional learning is self-deception, and what actually works.

item.title: 20 Habits With the Highest ROI in Life — Full Analysis & Fact Check
item.description: Complete breakdown of 20 habits for life improvement with fact checks, expert commentary, and practical applications for professional work.

item.title: The Radical Transparency Principle: Why Bridgewater Records Every Meeting
item.description: Ray Dalio, founder of the world's largest hedge fund, made every meeting accessible to every employee. Radical transparency and idea meritocracy became the foundation of Bridgewater Associates' extraordinary success.

item.title: Discipline Equals Freedom: Why Your Morning Routine Is Not a Chore
item.description: Jocko Willink's philosophy reveals why a strict morning routine, automated systems, and daily habits are not constraints — they are the very things that give you the freedom to focus on what matters most.

item.title: Start with Why: The Golden Circle That Separates Great Leaders from the Rest
item.description: Simon Sinek's Golden Circle reveals why Apple, Martin Luther King Jr., and the Wright Brothers inspired millions while others with better resources failed. People don't buy what you do — they buy why you do it.

item.title: The Courage to Be Flawed: What Brené Brown Taught Me About Quality Leadership
item.description: Brené Brown discovered that the best leaders are not perfect — they are brave enough to be vulnerable. Here is what that means for quality management and building a culture of trust.

item.title: The Bob Iger Strategy: Buy Your Competitors, Trust Your People
item.description: Bob Iger transformed Disney from an aging brand into the global entertainment king by acquiring competitors and trusting creative talent. Three lessons on leadership, competition, and the power of trust.

item.title: Tony Hsieh and Zappos: We Are Not a Shoe Company
item.description: Three extraordinary customer service stories from Zappos prove that the best marketing is not what you say about your brand — it is what your customers say about you.

item.title: The Peter Principle: Why Your Best People Keep Failing
item.description: Dr. Laurence J. Peter introduced the Peter Principle in 1969. This infographic-based exploration explains why competence gets promoted to incompetence and how companies can break the hierarchical trap.

item.title: The Architecture of Time — A Pyramid of Academic Productivity
item.description: An academic productivity pyramid reveals the brutal reality of how much focused writing time survives each week. From the inbox avalanche at the bottom to the protected writing block at the top.

item.title: Just Say No — The Power of Radical Focus
item.description: In 1997, Apple was 90 days from bankruptcy. Steve Jobs returned and cut 70% of the product line to a simple 2×2 grid. A story about the power of saying no.

item.title: The Evolution of Quality Management - From Craftsmanship to Global Supply Chain
item.description: A bilingual journey through the evolution of quality management - from craftsmanship to global supply chain collaboration.

item.title: The Ritz-Carlton's $2,000 Rule
item.description: How the Ritz-Carlton's $2,000 empowerment rule proves that trust is the most powerful management tool — and why every leader should empower their front-line teams.

item.title: Building Sustainable Supplier Management Systems
item.description: A structured approach to establishing supplier management systems that deliver consistent, long-term quality excellence across diverse manufacturing regions — from APAC challenges to global standards.

item.title: The Cost of Silence: Ford's Traffic Light System
item.description: How Alan Mulally's traffic light system at Ford Motor Company reveals the power of psychological safety in building honest quality cultures.
